teal-ink.note: Light-scheme accent. Hue is a pragmatic default, not a trademark; a future palette setting may replace it.

teal-mint.note: Dark-scheme accent. Reads as illumination against the dark field rather than as ink.

desk-light.note: Catppuccin Latte base. The lowest surface in the light scheme; nothing sits behind it.

desk-dark.note: Catppuccin Mocha mantle. The lowest surface in the dark scheme.

ink-light.note: Primary text in the light scheme. Never pure black; the desk metaphor has no ink that harsh.

ink-dark.note: Primary text in the dark scheme. Never pure white.

rule-light.note: The 1px divider that does the structural work shadows would do in a more decorative system.

alarm-light.note: Destructive confirmation and validation failure only. Never decorative.

display.purpose: The rare large moment; never used for chrome.

title.purpose: The workhorse heading: resume name on a card, active block title, empty-state heading.

body.purpose: Form field values and dialog prose.

label.purpose: Every button and menu item, in sentence case.

eyebrow.purpose: Section labels in the block rail; uppercase at 0.09em tracking.

caption.purpose: Counts and positional readouts; carries tabular figures.

body-small.purpose: Supporting text and every timestamp in the app; carries tabular figures.

extensions.fontNote: Inter variable (weights 100-900, opsz axis) ships inside the app at frontend/resume-builder-frontend/assets/fonts/Inter-Variable.ttf, the same file the resume templates use. Declared in src/renderer/App.css with font-display: block, and injected into the help page's iframe by HelpDialog.tsx. No webfont is fetched at runtime.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Survives only in the template picker. Not available to new work: a border or tone change says the same thing in both schemes.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Duration for every hover and selection state change: transform, box-shadow, border-color.

layout.name: sheet-grid
layout.purpose: The main screen grid of A4 sheets. Reflows by window width; the app's 1200px minimum window keeps it at four or more columns.

layout.name: panel-separator
layout.purpose: The draggable divider between resizable panes in the edit screen, filled with the rule color.

layout.name: rail-row-min
layout.purpose: Minimum pointer target for block rail rows, kept despite dense typography.

layout.name: sheet-aspect
layout.purpose: A4. Any container holding a page preview takes the page's proportion instead of imposing its own.

narrative.overview:
The hero of every screen is the document, not the application. The interface is the desk surface underneath a sheet of paper: level, matte, unhurried, and deliberately less interesting than the thing lying on it. Every screen in this app exists to hold a resume steady while someone works on it, and the screen that competes with the resume for attention has failed at its only job.

This is why the color system is built as a graded stack of desk tones rather than a single background: desk under everything, paper for the surfaces that carry content, editor for the working panel, card-well and backdrop for the recesses a PDF sits in. Depth in this system is a change in tone, not a shadow. The palette is Catppuccin-derived (Latte in light, Mocha in dark) and its accent is a muted teal chosen pragmatically, not a trademark. That accent is replaceable; the restraint is not. A future palette setting may swap every hue in this file, and the system must survive that swap without redesign, which is only true if no rule here depends on the hue itself.

The product's users arrive after long absences, often years, and never to admire the app. They are mid-application, switching between a vacancy posting and this window. The system therefore prizes legibility, a stable spatial model between visits, and the absence of anything that must be learned twice. Ornament is not suppressed because ornament is bad; it is suppressed because it would be aimed at the wrong object.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal depth, not shadow depth: surfaces separate by lightness step and a 1px rule.
One accent, used sparingly, on the action the user came to take.
Material Design as substrate, not as personality — the app reads as quiet, not as a Material demo.
The PDF is the only element allowed to look like a physical object.
Every string is a translation key; no layout may assume the width of English.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue in the system, and it never appears on a surface the user is not being asked to act on. If a screen has two teal things competing, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Replaceable-Hue Rule
rules.body: No rule in this system may depend on the accent being teal. The accent's role and scarcity are invariants; its hue is a default. A user-selectable palette must be able to replace every value in the frontmatter without invalidating a single line of this document.

rules.name: The Two-Scheme Rule
rules.body: Every color decision ships in both schemes or it does not ship. A value added to colors.light without its colors.dark counterpart is a bug, not a work in progress.

rules.name: The Bundled-Face Rule
rules.body: The interface font ships inside the app and loads from disk with font-display: block. A local file resolves in milliseconds, so blocking costs nothing and avoids a flash of fallback metrics; a webfont URL would break the product's offline promise outright.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Buttons and menu items are sentence case. Uppercase labels were the framework default, not a decision, and they cost Russian words their shape, since Cyrillic has less ascender/descender variety to survive the flattening.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes in place while the user watches, and any timestamp that sits in a column of other timestamps, uses tabular figures. This is carried by the body-small and caption roles, so it is inherited rather than remembered.

rules.name: The Translated-Width Rule
rules.body: No heading, label, or button may be sized on the assumption that its English string is the longest one. Russian runs longer; headings truncate with ellipsis and noWrap rather than wrapping the layout.

rules.name: The Dark-Bloom Rule
rules.body: Light text on the dark scheme is rendered with -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased. Identical weights bloom on a dark field and read a step heavier than they are; the thinner rasterization takes that step back off.

rules.name: The Window-Not-Device Rule
rules.body: This is a desktop app. Layout responds to container width through fluid grids and resizable panels; it does not branch on device breakpoints, and there is no mobile layout to maintain.

rules.name: The Persisted-Geometry Rule
rules.body: Anything the user physically drags — window size, splitter positions, preview zoom — is saved and restored. Returning to a layout you left is part of the product's promise of ownership.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface that is not hovered, dragged, open, or focused casts no shadow. If a new component needs a shadow to be findable, its tone or its rule is wrong.

rules.name: The Both-Schemes-Visible Rule
rules.body: Every state change must be perceptible in both light and dark. A shadow alone never satisfies this, because shadow is nearly invisible on a dark field — pair it with a tone or border change, or use tone alone.

rules.name: The Paper Exception
rules.body: The rendered PDF page is the one element permitted to read as a physical object sitting above its surface. It earns this because it is literally the document. Nothing else in the interface may borrow the treatment.

rules.name: The Radius-Tracks-Size Rule
rules.body: Radius scales with the element: 4px inline, 8px grouped, 12px container. A 12px radius on a button or a 4px radius on a card is a mistake, not a variant.

rules.name: The Square-Paper Exception
rules.body: The resume sheet on the main screen has no radius at all. It is the one element that is a document rather than a container, and paper does not have rounded corners. The exception is the sheet only; every container around it still follows the radius rule.

dos: Do separate surfaces with tone and a 1px rule, in the order desk → paper → editor → well/backdrop.
Do keep the accent scarce and tied to the single action a region is asking for.
Do declare new form UI in backend/src/main/resources/screens/*.json and render it through the existing registry.
Do pass every user-visible string through a translation key, and size layout for the longer Russian string.
Do persist anything the user physically drags or zooms.
Do set new text from one of the eight type roles; a one-off fontSize in an sx prop is how a ramp dies.
Do use tabular-nums for any numeric readout that updates in place.
Do verify both schemes before calling a state change done.

Do write dates the way a person would: relative inside a week, a plain calendar date after it, and never a clock time in a list. The backend formats the phrase and sends it ready to render, so the strings stay in the translation files with every other string.
donts: Don't write a raw hex value in a component. colors.ts is the only place color exists.
Don't let a shadow be the sole signal of a state change — it disappears in dark mode.
Don't give a resting surface a shadow.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, a gradient, or a decorative illustration. The document supplies all the visual interest this app needs.
Don't add a CSS feature to a resume template because it works in the app — templates render through openhtmltopdf, which supports a limited CSS subset and must be verified by rendering.
Don't build a bespoke React component when a registered field type fits.
Don't write a rule that depends on the accent being teal.
Don't add a second type family, an italic, or a weight outside 400-600. Inter alone carries every role.
Don't reference a font by URL, from Google Fonts or anywhere else. The face ships in the bundle or it does not ship.
Don't wrap a document preview in a well of a different proportion. The container takes the page's aspect ratio or there is no container.
